title: 2018 HMMT February Geometry Problem 2
statement: Points \(A, B, C, D\) are chosen in the plane such that segments \(A B, B C, C D, D A\) have lengths \(2,7,5\), 12 , respectively. Let \(m\) be the minimum possible value of the length of segment \(A C\) and let \(M\) be the maximum possible value of the length of segment \(A C\). What is the ordered pair \((m, M)\) ?

solutions.text:
Answer: \((7,9)\)
By the triangle inequality on triangle \(A C D, A C+C D \geq A D\), or \(A C \geq 7\). The minimum of 7 can be achieved when \(A, C, D\) lie on a line in that order. By the triangle inequality on triangle \(A B C\), \(A B+B C \geq A C\), or \(A C \leq 9\). The maximum of 9 can be achieved when \(A, B, C\) lie on a line in that order. This gives the answer \((7,9)\).
